lens: BIRTHS AT SCALE FOR THE HILL-CLIMBER: "R3-LEDGER". R3's nightly Opus 5.5 architect writes many FREE, forward-only ledger records a night: event-level atoms (headline and summary lexicons, 8-K item sets, source, hour and word-count sets) crossed with the lane's control streams and the non-price grid features. They cost no false-pass budget, no settlement, no data request and no per-event model call. They feed one consumer built for them: EVL-META-W-O1 and EVL-META-W-ON, the wide hill-climbers. These are PREREG-EVL-8's MRL-EB with two changes: an overdispersion-robust posterior, and a rolling WINDOW of awake records with a forward-only futility/stale exit. The search space grows by about 200 records a week with no upper bound. The awake family stays at or under the calibrated 2,600 sub-rules, and one 0.13 charge per run covers every record ever auditioned. The calibration forced one decision. The records must NOT join EVL-8's frozen meta-learners as s7.3 "ledger experts": they do not raise its false passes, but they spend its single budget-held run on noise.
design:
R3-LEDGER: ONE DESIGN, TWO PARTS. (H) The records economy: harness only, free, no seat, no charge, no captain step at night. (S) EVL-META-W-O1 and -ON: one new pre-registered file, two seats charged PREREG-EVL-6's 0.13 per run. The records' only consumer is S.

0. THE DECISION THE CALIBRATION FORCED, stated first
- PREREG-EVL-8 s7.3 lets "harness H6" ledger rules join EVL-META-O1/-ON as LEDGER EXPERTS, oldest registration first, up to the 1,535 cap.
- Measured with EVL-8's own generator and EVL-6's frozen screen, imported byte-identical. Script: calib_ledger.py at the corner cell.
- Births-shaped records (event-level atoms whose events lean to a home sector and to volatile or quiet names, as real lexicons do) filled the frozen family to about 1,500 sub-rules.
  - Run-1 false passes did NOT rise: 0.070 +- 0.015 (97% of runs ended by 2,000 sessions), against 0.103 +- 0.018 with no ledger.
  - The null pick rate DOUBLED: 10.8% of sessions against 5.7%.
  - The run was spent 2.7x sooner: median 103 sessions to the 22nd block against 274.
- The lane's budget holds about one run per EVL-8 version (EVL-8 s6.6: PREREG-EVL-6's second runs draw first). So the run IS the whole charge. On EVL-8's own true grid rule, births in the family cut run-1 power:
  - +60 bp: from 0.42 to 0.26.
  - +40 bp: from 0.25 to 0.07.
- Decision, recorded by amendment before EVL-META's first pick:
  - The judge's H6 does not ship. R3-LEDGER ships in its place, and its records are not s7.3 ledger experts. This is the reading that trades less (EVL-8 s15).
  - EVL-8's family stays as registered: grid + program experts + PX record experts.
  - The config flag `ledger.feeds_evl8` (default false) is the captain's alternative, priced above.
- For the same reason, the architect may no longer register non-seatable Program-row specs. A record is a ledger line. A Program-row record would join EVL-META as a program expert.

PART H: THE RECORDS ECONOMY
New file league/events/ledger.py; changes to births.py, store.py, house.py and report.py. All behind ci.py's wall.

H1 STREAMS
- A record is a FILTER of one registered control's real-money reading, book.picks(lane, s, D, decided_at=tau): every eligible event of the family, one per issuer, with the control's own 5-session cooldown.
- LEDGER_STREAMS (all v1):
  - O1: EVL-CTRL-NEWS-ALL-O1, EVL-CTRL-8K-ALL-O1, EVL-CTRL-ERN-ALL-O1.
  - ON: EVL-CTRL-NEWS-DAY-ON, EVL-CTRL-NEWSPM-ON, EVL-CTRL-8K-ON.
- Never EVL-CTRL-ERN-UNDER-ON: its selection reads a 15:29 reaction, which is a price.
- Never a PREREG-EVL-8 row (EVL-8 s4.4).
- A record writes no intent and needs no print, bar, settlement or model call. Its members' outcomes are the stream's own settled rows.

H2 CATALOG v1: atoms, event-level only
Each atom reads only the stream pick event's own row, as stored before tau.
- hl: {"any":[1-12 phrases]} over the stored headline. A phrase is 1-6 words of [a-z0-9&'.-], at most 40 characters, matched as a case-insensitive whole-word regex \b w1\s+w2 ... \b. News streams only.
- sm: the same over the stored summary. News streams only.
- items: {"any":[8-K items]} or {"all":[2-3 items]} over filings.items, from ITEMS_8K. 8-K and ERN streams.
- src: {"any":[sources]}, lower-cased. News streams.
- hours: {"any":[0-23]}, the knowable hour in New York. Any stream.
- words: {"min":a,"max":b}, the headline's word count, 1 <= a <= b <= 60. News streams.

REFUSED by the grammar (it has no field for them):
- issuer-sticky atoms: SIC, exchange, name, ticker, index;
- anything price- or volume-derived: prev_close, adv20, sigma60, bars, marks, reactions, gaps;
- outcomes and looks;
- another program's selection.

GRID PARTNERS ("g:<f>"): the non-price features of EVL-8 s7.3, read as it reads them: s>=1, s>=2, s=3, s<=-1, smiss, raised, lowered, bz, other, the six HOUR buckets, cov0, cov1-3, cov4+.

H3 LINES
The answer is {"specs":[as today, seatable only],"ledger":[...]} with three line kinds:
- {"kind":"atoms","v":1,"atoms":[{"name":"A-..","type":..,<body>,"why":"one line, its literature"}]}
- {"kind":"cross","v":1,"atoms":[..],"streams":[..],"with":["none"|"g:<f>",..]}. Expands deterministically, atoms x streams x with in that order.
- {"kind":"records","v":1,"records":[{"stream":..,"where":[["atom",n],["atom",n2]|["grid",f]]}]}

A RECORD is (stream, 1-2 terms), with at least one term an atom.

CANONICAL FORM
- Atom: its body with lists sorted, de-duplicated and lower-cased. sha256 over the body only. Id "A-"+sha[:10]. The proposed name is kept beside it (A95's doctrine).
- Record: terms sorted, atoms referred to by id. sha256 over {stream, terms}. Id "L-"+sha[:12].

The House appends only ACCEPTED canonical lines, in the night's one append:
- the accepted spec lines;
- one atoms line;
- "recs" lines of up to 37 records each (216 bytes a record; cost_night.py).
The gateway route (desk.mjs: 12 lines an append, 8 KB a line, 256 KB a file) holds about 400 records a night. No gateway change.

H4 THE VALIDATOR (ledger.validate)
Code, in order. Every figure is an outcome-free count under births' SQLite authorizer.
(a) Grammar and catalog. At most 12 new atoms a night; an atom proposed again with the same sha reuses the registered one.
(b) SUPPLY, over the RECORDED sessions of the last 20 (at least 3; SUP-3's denominator):
  - mean >= 3 selected events a session;
  - present on >= 50% of those sessions;
  - <= 50% of the stream's events.
  Today's record rule needs 20 stored sessions (births.py `facts.complete`), so it refuses every record until about Nov 13.
(c) DUPLICATES: the Jaccard of the selected events over those sessions must be < 0.8 against:
  - every registered program;
  - every registered record of the same stream;
  - every record accepted earlier that night;
  - every non-price grid single and pair evaluated on the stream's events.
(d) R_NIGHT = 20 accepted records per auction a night, taken in the answer's order (the architect's prior, outcome-free). The rest are refused with "night cap" and may be proposed again.
(e) CHARGE 0.
(f) A Program-row spec with seatable false is refused.

H5 THE NIGHT'S CALL
- births.py's one Opus 5.5 call, with model, effort low, streaming, LOST and the re-run rule all unchanged.
- MAX_TOKENS 6,000 -> 9,000.
- Rendered prompt <= 30,000 characters; the facts' lists are truncated deterministically.
- NIGHT_USD $0.25 unchanged. Worst case $0.242; typical $0.10-0.14 (cost_night.py).
- PARSE_VERSION 5.
- The prompt gains THE LEDGER section: the catalog, the line kinds, two valid examples, rules (b)-(d), and this instruction: "propose event types the published literature links to next-session returns, cite it in why, ranked by your prior; prefer atoms no record covers; records are free". Examples to cite: Womack 1996 (analyst actions); Brav and Lehavy 2003 (price targets); Ikenberry, Lakonishok and Vermaelen 1995 (buybacks); Michaely, Thaler and Womack 1995 (dividends); Loughran and Ritter 1995 (offerings); Tetlock 2011 (stale news).
- FACTS gain, as counts only:
  - each ledger stream's events per recorded session;
  - the 300 most frequent headline 1-3-grams, with stop words removed and no symbol, date or id;
  - each registered atom's hits per session on each stream;
  - the 50 most frequent 8-K item pairs;
  - META-W's window counts.
- FACTS_DENY gains mrl_ledger and mrl_w_*.

H6 TABLES (additive; SCHEMA_VERSION unchanged)
- ledger_atoms(atom PK, sha UNIQUE, type, body, name, why, night, seq, line, committed_at, received_at, registered_at)
- ledger_rules(rule PK, sha UNIQUE, stream, auction, terms, night, seq, pos, committed_at, received_at, registered_at). registered_at is the later of GitHub's commit time and the House's receipt. Ties break by seq, then pos.
- mrl_ledger(file, day, auction, rule, ciks_json, run, written_at; PK file, day, auction, rule). Written once in the decision's transaction.
- mrl_w_window(file, auction, rule, joined_day, left_day, why).
- Rows are never rewritten; a change is a new record.

H7 MEMBERSHIP: forward-only, the one rule
At a META-W decision of (D, X) at tau, record r of stream s gives a member m of (D, X) (EVL-8 s7.2) when all of these hold:
- s tags m;
- s's pick event e of m's issuer at tau has knowable_at(e) > registered_at(r);
- every term holds on e's fields as stored before tau. A grid partner is read by EVL-8 s7.3's reading. A missing field fails the term.
A catch-up reads the same stored rows and writes the same rows.

H8 REPORT AND ALARMS (counts only; the no-leaderboard test covers every ledger table)
- Report: records proposed, accepted, refused by reason and registered, by stream; the window's registered, waiting, awake and left counts; the night's cost.
- Alarms:
  - no record accepted on 3 session nights running;
  - an awake record with no mrl_ledger write;
  - more than 500 waiting (info).

PART S: EVL-META-W-O1 / EVL-META-W-ON
S1 Programs, v1
- O1: open of D to close of D. ON: close of D to the next open.
- Learning band, open cap 8. Whole shares at PREREG-EVL-2's limit, PREREG-EVL-1 s5's costs and TRADABLE, A72's 5-session rule.
- Controls: the free records -O1-POOL and -ON-POOL.
- Each counts only its own picks of events knowable after REGISTERED_AT_W.

S2 Members, features, marks and member outcomes: EVL-8 s7.2-7.3 VERBATIM BY REFERENCE
- Read from EVL-8's mrl_pool when its live decision wrote them; otherwise built by the same rule from the same stored times.
- META-W writes its own mrl_w_* tables and never an EVL-8 table.

S3 Family
- EVL-8's grid, program experts and PX record experts, as EVL-8 defines them at each decision.
- Plus THE WINDOW: the awake R3-LEDGER records of X's streams.
- CAP: base + window <= 2,600 sub-rules, the largest awake family calibrated (2,594-2,659). This gives W_X of about 1,675 (O1) and 1,430 (ON).

S4 State
- EVL-8 s7.4 verbatim, plus per sub-rule Q2_j = sum w R_js^2 / V_js and NW_j = sum w, over the same sessions and weights.
- A record's sums start empty at its join.

S5 Decision
- phi_j = max(1, (K0 + Q2_j - G_j^2/A_j) / (K0 + NW_j - 1)), with K0 = 10.
- prec_j = A_j/phi_j + TAU^-2; m_j = (G_j/phi_j)/prec_j; LCB_j = m_j - Z_W prec_j^-1/2.
- This is quasi-likelihood dispersion (Wedderburn 1974, Biometrika 61(3); McCullagh and Nelder 1989). A sub-rule whose blocks scatter beyond the model (a sector's shock, a beta tilt) loses precision by its own scatter.
- AWAKE, QUALIFIED (-cbar_D + LCB > 0), WARM 10, the walk and the writes: EVL-8 s7.5 verbatim, with why "mrlw".

S6 The window, at each decision before the walk
(1) LEAVE for good when either:
  - FUTILE: NB >= 20 and m + 1.0 sd <= cbar_D; or
  - STALE: NB >= 250 and never qualified.
(2) JOIN the oldest waiting records (registered_at, then seq, then pos) while fewer than W_X are awake.
A record that left never returns, and proposing it again is refused as a duplicate by H4(c).

S7 Constants
K 16; H 60; TAU 0.0030; SF 0.0020; Z_W 3.0; K0 10; HURDLE 0; MINB 3; WARM 10; variance floor 0.015^2; winsorization +-10%; imputation -0.30 after 3 sessions; cap 2,600; EXIT_NB 20; EXIT_Z 1.0; STALE_NB 250.

S8 Money
- EVL-8 s4 and s7.7: the guards, the late passes and every wall.
- Learning ROOM after every earlier file's rows and before R3's seatable births (A101). Probe 14.
- Its own scheduler slot (A120): decide-open-mw after decide-open-px8, and decide-close-mw after decide-close-meta8, 20 s each. A part not finished in its bound is never traded at that auction.

S9 Judge
- PREREG-EVL-6 s1-3 AS FROZEN, word for word: CAP 8, in runs, each run charged when it starts and drawn in registration order.
- Charge per run: max(0.13, the measured worst plausible) = 0.13. Total 0.26 at registration.
why_it_compounds:
1. It turns ideas into forward evidence for free, with no limit on how many ideas get searched. Every session night adds up to 20 new event-type records per auction, about 200 a week. That is 2,400 auditioned by week 12 (growth.py). Each costs no false-pass budget, no settlement, no data request and no per-event model call. One 0.13 run charge covers every record the window ever holds.

2. The hill-climber is patient, so its one charged run waits for something real.
- With the overdispersion term, EVL-META-W picks in only 1.4-1.5% of sessions under the null, even with about 1,100-1,800 awake records.
- At the same corner, the frozen meta-learner with births in its family picks in 10.8%; without overdispersion the window picks in 46% (pilot).
- So its run reaches the 22nd block only after a median of 1,138-1,538 sessions under the null, and a record that turns out real in week 8 still has the run.
- With a +60 bp births record registered at session 200, run 1 passes 0.40 against the oracle's 0.36: a fixed program registered with the gem, which knows which record it is. At +40 bp it is 0.13 against 0.13. Under a one-run budget, that is about all the money can buy.

3. Selection is pre-registered and forward-only. No designer, architect or captain reads a per-record figure: records are machine-only and the no-leaderboard test covers them. Records that cannot clear the bar leave by the futility rule, the next registered records take their place, and capital goes to the record with the highest lower bound at every decision.

4. It protects the frozen bets. EVL-8's meta-learners keep their calibrated family and their one run for EVL-8's own price records. Births in that family would cut its run-1 power on its own +60 bp rule from 0.42 to 0.26.

5. Breadth tracks the market. The architect reads only outcome-free supply facts: headline n-gram counts, atom hit counts and item pairs. It extends coverage toward event types the published literature links to returns, including new ones as headline vocabulary and the season change, and the validator keeps only what has supply and is new (Jaccard < 0.8).

6. The loop runs without hands. Nightly proposing, validation, registration, joining, exiting, deciding and screening are all code. Alarms cover stalls.
events_per_session_and_cost:
FREE RECORDS
- Up to 20 accepted per auction a night, about 200 a week across both auctions (growth.py).
- The awake window stays at or under W_X: about 1,675 for O1 and 1,430 for ON. In the calibration the mean awake life was about 76 sessions.
- Records produce no real-money events themselves.

EVL-META-W REAL-MONEY EVENTS
- Under the null: about 0.16-0.18 shadow picks a session, with picks in 1.4-1.5% of sessions (calib_ledger.py, corner cell). That is nearly no learning-size exposure.
- When a record carries an edge: up to 16 shadow picks a session (K). Real lots are capped at 8 open per program at learning and 14 at Probe, after ROOM and cash. The book is cash-bound at about 27-31 Probe lots in all (KEPT-1019h).
- In the +60 bp power cells, picks came in 46-54% of sessions at about 6-7 a session averaged over the whole run, and the picks' true mean was +58-59 bp. Two promoted META-W rows could supply Done's ">= 50 each" in a few weeks of Probe sessions.

METERED COST (all inside A102's $5 a day)
- The births night stays capped at NIGHT_USD $0.25. Worst case $0.242 at a 30,000-character prompt and 9,000 output tokens. Typical $0.10-0.14 (2,600-4,100 output tokens with thinking at 1,500-3,000; cost_night.py). Today's night is about $0.03 (A109), so the added spend is about $0.07-0.11 a night.
- META-W's decisions add $0: CPU only. Membership for at most 2,600 sub-rules over at most 900 members is under a second.
- The nightly validator's Jaccards over about 20 sessions x 1,500 events take seconds.
- mrl_ledger holds one row per (auction, record, session): at most about 3,100 rows a session.

FALSE-PASS BUDGET
- 0.26 at registration: two runs at 0.13.
- LEFT after EVL-6, -7, -8 and -9 is 0.74 with no birth, or 0.35 if A104's three are seated (EVL-9's newest text). META-W's two seats fit before A104's births or instead of two of them; that order is the captain's.
- Null run turnover is 0.33 runs started per 1,000 sessions (T 4,000), so later runs draw slowly.
calibration:
Every figure is synthetic. Scripts are in /home/bwoods1998/Work/.ltcm-main/goal-2026-10-19/evl10/ledger/ (SHA256SUMS there). Seeds start at 193,000,001 and are fresh.

THE SIMULATOR
- EVL-8's final generator (calib_meta_b8.py) and EVL-6's frozen screen in runs (meta_final8.py `screen_runs`, which uses calib_final.py, sha e35e649d) are imported UNCHANGED. Their sha256s ff313e3e and 7fcd7afb equal the copies at tag prereg-evl-8.
- `selftest`: with no ledger the arrays equal calib_meta_b8.simulate bit for bit.
- Atoms are drawn from a separate RNG stream so the frozen draws are untouched. They are event-level, with prevalence 2-25%, kappa 0.5 of each atom's events in a home sector, and a volatility tilt gamma ~ N(0, 0.6).
- Records are an atom alone or an atom with one of 15 non-price grid partners, kept when supply is >= 3 a session. 25 register per session, and each starts empty at its join (forward-only).
- Base family: wide2, 815 sub-rules (widths.py).

THE WORLD
- CORNER is EVL-8's worst plausible cell: beta_day 0.3, style co-movement 0.6%, t(3)-body crash days clustered in high volatility, phi_day 0.20, rho_day 0.15, left skew, a 20 bp AR(0.97) drift, no issuer effect.
- Power cells use the base world.

prereg_clauses:
PREREG-EVL-W, "the wide hill-climbers"; the captain numbers it
- Registration: REGISTERED_AT_W is the latest of three times (A92's method): the commit time, the client clock after the tag push, and GitHub's push activity. It freezes after EVL-8. Its programs count only events knowable after it.
- Programs: S1-S9 of the design, verbatim, with S7's constants fixed from the synthetic calibration only:
  - Z_W 3.0; K0 10; cap 2,600; EXIT_NB 20; EXIT_Z 1.0; STALE_NB 250;
  - EVL-8's K 16, H 60, TAU 0.0030, SF 0.0020, MINB 3 and WARM 10.
- EVL-8 s7.2-7.5 are incorporated by reference, with only the overdispersion term and the window changed.
- Judge: PREREG-EVL-6 s1-3 as frozen at tag prereg-evl-6, CAP 8, in runs. Each run is charged 0.13 when it starts and drawn in registration order after every earlier file. A run whose charge the budget cannot hold does not start, and the version stays in learning.
- Records counted: a ledger record counts only at decisions after its own registered_at, and only for events knowable after that time. Its sums start empty at its join, and a record that has left never returns.
- Machine-only: no figure from mrl_w_*, mrl_ledger or ledger_* is reported, read by births or read by any designer. The no-leaderboard test applies.
- Ambiguity: the reading less likely to pass or that trades less, fixed before the first pick. A later resolution is a new version.
- Calibration record: evl10/ledger/ with its SHA256SUMS, copied to docs/prereg/evl-w/ at the freeze.

(2) R3 v3: K seatable specs as today. Records only as ledger lines. R_NIGHT 20 per auction. The record rate is read over the recorded sessions. MAX_TOKENS 9,000, the prompt <= 30,000 characters, NIGHT_USD $0.25, PARSE_VERSION 5.
(3) Seat order against A104: META-W's two seats (0.26) before A104's three births (0.39), or A104's three registered as free records. The captain chooses and states the cost.

programs.py: rows EVL-META-W-O1/ON v1 and their POOL records with REGISTERED_AT_W; book.py ROOM after every earlier file's rows and before seatable births; constitution money row event.max_open_w.learning 8 (bound 0-8).
Scheduler (A120, feat/scheduler): slots decide-open-mw and decide-close-mw after EVL-8's parts, 20 s bounds, receipts, and catch-ups decide-mw:<X>:<D> that write the same rows.
screen.py: META-W under PREREG-EVL-6 frozen in runs, its CONTROLS rows (POOL), and expected_false_passes counting 0.13 per run.
config: ledger.feeds_evl8 = false, with a test that EVL-8's family holds no l: sub-rule; events.ledger on/off flag for rollback.

report.py and daily_report.py: counts only (proposed, accepted, refused by reason, registered; window registered, waiting, awake, left; night cost); the no-leaderboard test extended to every ledger and mrl_w_* table.
evl_health: no record accepted on 3 session nights; an awake record with no mrl_ledger write; window waiting > 500 (info).

Tests: canonical sha stability; cross expansion order; supply and Jaccard on a synthetic store; a record registered at t has no members before t (live equals catch-up); phi formula against calib_ledger.py's; window cap and exit order; earlier files' intents byte-identical with the ledger on and off; a dry-run night on a synthetic answer within $0.25.
risks: The generator is EVL-8's synthetic world. Real lexicons may concentrate in sectors or issuers more than the stress cell (kappa 0.9, gamma sd 1.0, issuer effects 1%) or recur on a few meme names. The grammar refuses issuer-sticky atoms, and the overdispersion term discounts scatter, but a live share of sessions with picks far above 1.5% would show the mismatch.

Z_W 3.0's per-run figure is 0.085 +- 0.020 by 4,000 sessions with 46% of runs ended (98.5% past the 22nd block). The tail is bounded only by the low alpha of the later looks (0.006 and 0.001). Z 2.5 is the fully measured fallback: 0.090 +- 0.017 with 99.7% ended, but lower run-1 power (0.27 against 0.40 at +60 bp).

The budget binds. Two runs cost 0.26 of the 0.35-0.74 left. A second run may never start, so run-1 power is what counts. A +40 bp record is found in run 1 only 0.13 of the time, the same as an oracle.

pi is unknown and cannot be learned blind. If no record carries an after-cost edge, META-W trades almost nothing and costs its charge. Its false-pass exposure is the measured per-run figure, under 0.13.
Futility and stale exits can retire a slow true edge: a +40 bp gem left 23% of the time at Z 3.0 with stale 250, and 51-56% with stale 120.

Not feeding EVL-8's meta-learners departs from the H6 path its text names. The amendment must be recorded before EVL-META's first pick, or the reading is contested. If the flag is flipped, EVL-META's run-1 power on its own rules falls (0.42 to 0.26 at +60 bp).

Architect quality: Opus may propose near-duplicates or low-supply lexicons. The validator prunes them (supply, Jaccard < 0.8, R_NIGHT), so the cost is wasted tokens, not false passes. Headline template changes shift supply forward-only.
Seat order collides with A104: its three day-news births registering first at 01:00Z Oct 24 would leave only 0.35, enough for both META-W seats but nothing else. This needs the captain's order.

Build dependency: META-W needs EVL-8's mrl.py (release 1019j) and the scheduler slot (1019i). Records registered before META-W's code ships start their state only at their join, so there is no loss of honesty, only time.
Storage and timing: about 3,100 mrl_ledger rows a session and a 20 s decision slot; a part that overruns is not traded at that auction (the reading that trades less).
